Are You Experienced?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1301 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Sources indicate that I must achieve internal consistency.
  • The gods decreed that I shall not be a translator, and I am grateful for that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Sources indicate that I must achieve internal consistency. —Edmund Husserl, turning an Erlebnis (Type I experience) into an Erfahrung (Type II experience).

The gods decreed that I shall not be a translator, and I am grateful for that. A direct translation from one language to another is a goal we can strive for, but rarely attain fully. The words of any particular language are rich in unique shades of meaning, allusions, emotional undertones, and cross-references to synonyms, which live lives of their own.

Sources indicate that homer called his hero Odysseus πολύτροπος (polytropos), literally “a man of many turns.” But being “of many turns” does not call forth useful associations in English, and so translators have struggled with—and argued with each other about—what to make of polytropos. Some render the idea as “endlessly cunning” (Mitchell, 2014), while others prefer “complicated” (Wilson, 2018). Neither hits the mark. One might as well try shrewd, crafty, clever, or inventive. “Endlessly cunning” is marred by the addition of the adverb, and “complicated” makes it sound like Odysseus needs therapy. “Complex” would have been a better choice. I prefer the phrase “a man of many devices” (Murray, 1919), which recognizes Odysseus’s rich and variable toolbox of survival skills, including those involving deception.

In a recent development, different languages emphasize and elaborate different concepts, whatever is notable in their natural and cultural context. We can marvel at some of these differences. Since Franz Boas (1911) suggested the Greenland Inuit have four different words for snow, others have grown the list, while still others have declared Boas’s observation a myth, one they find vexingly persistent. Other inter-language differences are less controversial, and some of these refer to psychological states. How many types of love are there? The Hebrew tradition counts four. What kinds of longing are there? Is the Portuguese saudade equivalent to the German Sehnsucht? On Seinfeld, Kramer asks George if he has ever yearned. “Yearned?” George replies. “I’ve craved!”.

Psychology can be understood as the science of behavior and experience. Both terms carry complexity, and the latter more so than the former. What, we ask, is an experience? It does not take a Ludwig Wittgenstein to see that this concept embraces many variants that may not even share a single common feature. To say that an experience is whatever one experiences is to kick the can down the road; it is a tautology.

In a recent development, when I asked A.I. Claude what an experience is, I received this response: “Experience (noun) has two main senses, and the difference matters.” Claude goes on to explain that one of these senses refers to a process or event, with a first-person involvement. A first kiss delivers this kind of experience. Another sense refers to accumulated knowledge or skill; the sort of thing you put on your résumé. The first sense is what is sometimes called lived experience, whereas the second sense goes further by demanding that something has been learned, something that contributes to the person’s σωφροσύνη (sophrosyne), or practical wisdom. Anyone can have a store of Type I (lived) experiences, but this does not make them “experienced.” The participle must be earned. To have lived experience may simply mean that one hasn’t died yet. To have Type II (empirical) experience means to have made active investments in life that can be cashed out to help reach one’s goals and enhance one’s well-being.

Sources indicate that explaining the conceptual difference between Type I and Type II experience in English requires space, patience, and some circumlocution. The German language offers a clean distinction between Erlebnis, ɛɐˈleːpnɪs, and Erfahrung, ɛɐ̯ˈfaːʁʊŋ. The difference between the two was elaborated by the philosophers Wilhelm Dilthey (1883) and Edmund Husserl (1900-1901), whose work is interesting to consider in light of today’s debates over epistemology (Krueger, 2026). Expressing a popular view, Aziz and Anjum (2025) suggest that the prevailing scientific ethos in psychology is limited and systematically biased by excluding, misrepresenting, and disadvantaging many human populations. What is silenced, according to this view, are the lived experiences existing in these populations. These lived experiences, it is further argued, must be given their due; they must be heard and respected. And so, the argument goes on, these lived experiences must be acknowledged as an alternative epistemology, a way of knowing things, a way of having “knowledges.” Authors arguing the line pursued by Aziz and Anjum differ in how far they wish to go. Some are willing to settle for a lived-experience epistemology being accepted as equivalent to the scientific theory-and-data epistemology. Others wish to see psychological science be remade in light of lived experiences. These writers view the traditional scientific epistemology as oppressive, colonialist, and exploitative.

Dilthey and Husserl would pause here. To them, Erlebnis (Experience Type I) and Erfahrung (Experience Type II) are equally essential to the human condition; they cannot be pitted against each other. What contemporary critics of conventional empirical science seem to miss is that Erlebnis cannot absorb Erfahrung. Being effortful, empirical, and hard-won, Erfahrung is the grounds for reasoned beliefs that can be put to the test, that can be modified or overturned by continued activity. Erfahrung remains a work in progress. An Erlebnis, by contrast, is registered, perhaps committed to memory, and then gradually lost. A tourist has Erlebnisse; a traveler gathers Erfahrungen. It is the difference between perception and cognition.

Science is Erfahrung tamed, structured, and refined into a systematic method. Well-designed studies are efficient ways of learning Nature’s secrets. We can have an Erlebnis when walking into the woods, but only by planting a garden, by experimenting with different seeds, and by pruning excess growth, can we come to have the kind of Erfahrung that allows us to explain things and to teach what we have learned. The rejection of science from the lived-experience perspective is a short-sighted endeavor. The most it can hope to achieve is a narrative. Listening to these narratives can be an Erlebnis, but what can it teach us?

In a recent development, once the difference between the two types of experience is understood, many familiar narratives appear in a new light. An ancient myth tells us that Adam and Eve had lovely Erlebnisse in the Garden of Eden. In the Land of Nod, they were forced to make Erfahrungen. With that, they became self-aware.

Note: The image above shows what Claude produced when asked to capture the concept of lived experience visually. The effort is interesting but not entirely satisfying since there are several dimensions (time, space, meaning) cross-cutting a scheme built on the idea of concentricity. I confirm that I never use AI to do my writing for me.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The RESET for Remission trial, presented at the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) Annual Meeting and published in The Lancet Regional Health Americas on October 1, found that more than half of adults with early onset type 2 diabetes entered remission after six months on a low calorie diet and supervised exercise program.

Early onset type 2 diabetes is when the condition is diagnosed before age 45.

Those with early onset type 2 diabetes may be at a higher risk of complications like long-term damage to the capillaries (microvascular complications), adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and earlier death.

Typical treatment for early onset type 2 diabetes is often a combination of lifestyle changes, like diet and exercise, and medications.

However, this latest study suggests that a supervised low calorie diet and exercise program may help some people with early onset type 2 diabetes enter remission.

The RESET for Remission trial included 96 adults from England and Canada who were between the ages of 18 and 45, had early onset type 2 diabetes, obesity, and were not on insulin treatment.

Industry observers note that the participants had an average age of 38 and an average body mass index (BMI) of 35.2 kg/m2. They were randomized into a control group that received usual care alone and the intervention group, which ate a low calorie diet and participated in supervised exercise programs.

During the first 12 weeks, participants in the intervention group followed an 800–900-calorie-per-day diet and completed twice-weekly supervised aerobic and resistance exercise sessions, along with one independent exercise session per week.

For weeks 13–24, they transitioned to a weight-maintenance diet and independent exercise.

Both groups were supervised by physicians, and the intervention group was also closely supervised by licensed dietitians.

The low calorie diet consisted of 30% protein, 50% carbohydrate, and 20% fat. Participants were also encouraged to drink at least 2 liters of calorie-free fluids per day and given access to a fiber-based laxative as needed.

It has been revealed that in the first two weeks, all meals were replaced with specially formulated nutritional products (Optifast). Then, in weeks 3–12, the participants maintained the same calorie intake but had more flexibility in their food choices.

Sources indicate that this second phase of the diet included one conventional meal per day, with daily intake targets that included protein, fruit, and vegetables. Typically, this meant 60 to 90 grams of protein from all sources combined, one portion of fruit, and two portions of non-starchy vegetables.

At the end of 24 weeks, 54% of the intervention group entered remission of type 2 diabetes, compared with only 4% in the control group. Researchers defined remission as an HbA1c level below 6.5% without glucose-lowering medication for at least 12 weeks.

According to recent reports, “This study proves what most physicians have advocated for quite some time. Clearly, diet and exercise can work to improve or even resolve diabetes,” David Cutler, MD, board certified family medicine physician at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline.

Cutler also added that this study provides a clear example of how difficult it can be to enter diabetes remission with diet and exercise alone. He stated that the small number of participants in the study also makes him wonder if these findings can be applied to all populations.

Another limitation of this study, as Cutler pointed out, was that the strict dietary limits imposed on study participants would be very difficult for the average adult to adhere to.

The study also followed participants for only six months, so it’s unclear how many would remain in remission over the longer term.

“It is worth trying diet and exercise first because they can work to achieve meaningful weight loss and remission of diabetes,” he mentioned.

It may be possible to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes by:.

The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) notes that losing 5%–7% of your body weight can help reduce your risk of type 2 diabetes.

Early onset type 2 diabetes is a growing matter worldwide, coinciding with the rise of obesity.

Industry observers note that research from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) projects that the number of people in the United States under age 20 with type 2 diabetes could reach 220,000 by 2060. This is an increase of 700%.

People diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at a younger age face more decades of living with the condition, along with a higher risk of developing complications earlier in life and reduced life expectancy. These complications can develop as early as midlife and include:.

Speak with a healthcare professional about your risk of type 2 diabetes and changes you might be able to make in order to prevent or delay diagnosis.

A later diagnosis can help reduce the risk of some complications of the condition.

Internet-famous bald eagle Shadow has endured an up-and-down 2026. From suffering the loss of a clutch of eggs to welcoming two chicks, and from losing his longtime partner to finding a upcoming friend, he’s had a tumultuous year.

Industry observers note that after the August death of Jackie, the female eagle he raised chicks with since 2018, Shadow began spending time with a 4-year-old female eagle named Kaydee (formerly KD1). Viewers of the 24/7 livestream of Shadow’s nest could easily spot Kaydee because of her double-banded legs—a silver ring on one leg and a lavender one on the other. The pair appeared chummy as they spent more time together, sharing stick-arranging duties, singing, and exchanging beaky kisses. An unexpected twist arrived this week with the appearance of an unknown female bald eagle spotted in the nest with Shadow.

Cameras spotted the unknown female in the nest in recent weeks, but this was the first time the eagle was joined by Shadow. On Monday afternoon, Shadow landed in the nest swiftly followed by the unknown female. The unknown female fiddled the nest sticks while vocalizing and Shadow appeared unbothered by her presence. Eagles will typically defend their nest from intruders so Shadow’s willingness to share his space with an eagle other than Kaydee surprised many viewers.

Shadow returned the nest solo later in the afternoon as the sun set over Substantial Bear Lake.

As this is nature, all we can do is sit back and see what unfolds. Mating season is approaching, so we have to wait and see if Shadow selects a new partner. Female eagles in Massive Bear Valley typically lay their first clutch of eggs in January. Tune in to Friends of Big Bear Valley’s (FOBBV) livestreams to follow the southern California eagles anytime.

Recent findings suggest that kaydee, formerly known as KD1, is a banded female bald eagle that has been spotted in Major Bear Valley following the death of Shadow’s former partner, Jackie. She was born in 2022, about 70 miles away from Big Bear Lake in the Prado Basin between Anaheim and Riverside, California. Coincidentally, her parents are also named Lucky and Ricky like Jackie’s parents, but they are a different eagle pair.

Kaydee was banded as part of the Orange County Water District’s work to track the eagles born in the area. These bands help biologists track and monitor the birds over time. Kaydee right now has a black spot on her head, but it may not be permanent. It’s possible that not all of her white feathers have come in or it could be tree sap or dirt. She also has two small bands on her legs. One is a small metal band, while the other is a lavender band with “KD1” on it.

In a recent development, kaydee is almost five years old, so she is just about ready to mate. She was recently spotted on FOBBV’s livestream inspecting the nest and has also been seen hanging out near Shadow. Flying around Significant Bear is completely normal behavior for young adult eagles at this time of year.

Industry observers note that in January, Jackie laid two eggs in the nest, but ravens destroyed them. She later laid two more eggs that hatched in April and named Luna and Sandy. The name Sandy is in honor of FOBBV’s former executive director Sandy Steers who died from cancer in February.

On July 17, Jackie was found injured on the ground near Dana Point Park, California. Cell phone video from a witness confirmed that she had an altercation with two other subadult eagles. She successfully fended off the other eagles by turning over and using her talons, but could not fly far away.

Sources indicate that she was transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for care, where she was diagnosed with severe anemia. Her anemia worsened during the first week of August, the Ojai Raptor Center said that she was in unstable condition on August 9. Her packed cell volume (PCV) fell below six percent, before rising to nine percent. Jackie died early in the morning on August 10. The necropsy did not reveal a single cause of death, and instead pointed to several factors including severe anemia, bird flu, blood clots in her wing and one kidney, and liver and lung abnormalities.

According to recent reports, A memorial service was held on September 5 in Fawnskin, California, along with a second celebration of life called Wings Over Big Bear on October 3. The event featured representatives from FOBBV, the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit. Tesla rates it at 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuously at 34.5 kV, with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA of peak power.

It’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027. That’s the same year Heron Power, the startup founded by Tesla’s former top engineer Drew Baglino, plans to start volume production of its own solid-state transformer, the Heron Link.

Patch: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center plans. We’ve updated the article with the new details.

According to recent reports, tesla first said it would build its own transformers in September 2025, when it unveiled Megapack 3 and Megablock. Megablock connects four Megapack 3 units to a transformer and switchgear, but Tesla shared next to nothing about the transformer itself.

It has been revealed that powercore is that missing piece. Tesla unveiled it today through its Tesla Megapack account on X:.

It has been revealed that introducing PowercoreSolid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak powerMade in America. Operating 2027 pic.twitter.com/sHxqnpWJrf.

About an hour later, Tesla followed up with a much longer post on X laying out the full spec sheet:.

It also packs a built-in solid-state medium-voltage breaker that Tesla says clears faults up to 1,000x faster than a conventional breaker. There’s no flammable oil, and it’s modular, so components can be serviced in the field without swapping the whole unit.

It has been revealed that tesla is pitching one product for three markets: battery storage, utility-scale solar, and 800 Vdc data centers. For Megablock, Powercore replaces the current two-step setup, where Megapack’s inverters output 480 V AC before a separate transformer steps it up to medium voltage. Tesla says that old architecture had twice the losses. For solar, Powercore works as a central inverter for today’s 1,500 Vdc arrays and upcoming 2,000 Vdc systems.

It has been revealed that tesla still hasn’t shared pricing, customers, or a factory location. It only states Powercore will be made in the US “of U.S. and imported parts” with first units operating in 2027.

The idea behind a solid-state transformer is simple enough. A typical solar or battery project uses low-voltage inverters to convert DC into AC, then a substantial oil-filled, iron-core transformer to step that up to grid voltage. A solid-state unit does both jobs with silicon carbide power electronics, which means less gear, a smaller footprint, and active control over voltage and frequency. That control is what “grid-forming” means: the unit can help hold the grid steady instead of just following it.

And with lead times on conventional transformers stretching into years as data centers and renewable projects pile into interconnection queues, there’s real demand for an alternative.

You can’t look at Powercore without thinking of Heron Power.

It has been revealed that baglino spent 18 years at Tesla and finished as SVP of powertrain and energy, in charge of batteries, motors, power electronics, and energy products. He left in April 2024 and introduced Heron Power in 2025 to build solid-state transformers.

He brought a lot of Tesla’s power electronics talent with him. As we reported when Tesla first unveiled its transformer plans, Heron hired engineers who led power electronics design for Powerwall 3, the next-gen Megapack, and Superchargers, along with the person who ran Tesla’s power electronics controls team for charging and energy products.

It has been revealed that since then, Heron has raised a $38 million Series A, a $140 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and a $60 million credit facility from J.P. Morgan and TriplePoint Capital. Former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn sits on its board, and Tesla co-founder JB Straubel is an investor.

It’s also building Heron Factory One, a 286,000-square-foot plant in Morgan Hill, California, designed to make 10,000 Heron Links a year. That’s over 40 GW of annual capacity, with commercial production planned for late 2027.

In a recent development, and the customers are lining up. Vantage reserved more than 1 GW for its data centers, Intersect reserved 1.5 GW, LG Energy Solution Vertech is integrating Heron Link with its US-made battery systems, and RWE signed a pilot to install Heron Links at a Texas battery storage site in April 2027. Baglino indicates Heron has 50 GW of orders in the pipeline.

Here’s how the two compare based on what each company has disclosed:.

According to recent reports, on paper, Powercore is the bigger box, and now it has the better numbers too. At 7.4 MW continuous, it carries about 50% more power per unit than the 5 MW Heron Link, and its 98.86% peak efficiency edges out Heron’s 98.6%. But Tesla’s figure is a peak number, and Heron doesn’t label its own as one, so it’s not quite apples to apples. Neither company has shared pricing.

Recent findings suggest that tesla is also going straight at Heron’s data center pitch. Powercore converts medium voltage directly to 800 Vdc, the rack architecture Nvidia is pushing, and Tesla says it’s working with Nvidia on 800 Vdc designs. Heron’s data center version does the same 34.5 kV AC to 800 VDC conversion with built-in storage, and data centers make up about a third of its business. Tesla’s answer to the storage piece is Megapack on the DC bus, and it says it already has 10 GWh of Megapack running at data centers.

This one is a little awkward for Tesla.

It has been revealed that A major chunk of the people who designed Tesla’s power electronics over the last decade now work at Heron, and the guy who ran the whole org is its CEO. Tesla’s energy business also lost its longtime leader, Mike Snyder, last month, according to the WSJ.

This is all wrong. Tesla started developing this 3 years ago. Before Heron. The team selling Powercore is same as Megapack that has a way larger customer base than Heron. To be fair, Tesla still has plenty of power electronics expertise. Its silicon carbide inverters are in millions of cars and every Megapack. And it has something Heron doesn’t: a massive installed base and a sales channel. Tesla says it’s almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027, and bundling Powercore into Megablock is an easy upsell. Plenty of developers will take the one-stop shop.

#5300. Latest Update: Why Gratitude Sometimes Backfires

Latest Update: Why Gratitude Sometimes Backfires

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • You can appreciate the people in your life and still dread being asked to announce it over dinner.
  • The cranberry sauce has made its annual appearance in the shape of the can it came from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

You can appreciate the people in your life and still dread being asked to announce it over dinner.

The turkey is carved. The cranberry sauce has made its annual appearance in the shape of the can it came from. Then someone says: “Let’s go around the table and say what we’re grateful for.”.

According to recent reports, forks pause midair. Eyes drift toward the mashed potatoes like they might offer an escape.

A cousin states something heartfelt and beautiful, and now the emotional bar has been raised to Olympic height.

In a recent development, am I grateful enough? Should I say something profound?

According to recent reports, gratitude rituals are meant to create warmth. And often they do. But psychologically, gratitude is a little more complicated than the greeting cards suggest.

It has been revealed that the benefits are real. A 2023 meta-analysis of 25 randomized controlled trials involving 6,745 participants found that expressing gratitude reliably improved happiness, life satisfaction, and psychological well-being compared with neutral activities.

But that doesn’t tell us everything about how gratitude feels in the moment.

In a recent development, in three experiments, psychologists examined people’s feelings after exercises such as recalling another person’s kindness or writing a gratitude letter they never sent. Alongside feeling moved and uplifted, the gratitude participants tended to report more indebtedness (and sometimes more feelings of guilt) than participants who did a neutral task.

It's like unwrapping a gift and realizing you didn’t bring one.

Gratitude can feel uplifting and slightly uncomfortable at the same time. It can carry a kind of social math: They gave + I received = Now I owe them.

That discomfort doesn’t necessarily mean something has gone wrong. Wanting to give something back can be part of caring for a relationship.

But if gratitude can make us feel both good and uncomfortable, what happens when the discomfort arrives from somewhere else entirely?

In a randomized study of 156 undergraduates, participants completed about 12 minutes of gratitude practice, mindful breath awareness, loving-kindness, or a neutral visualization exercise. Those who practiced gratitude did report more positive emotion.

But then researchers introduced a stressor: Participants had to submerge their hand in a bucket of ice-cold water while a researcher in a lab coat stood nearby, observing with the emotional warmth of a marble statue — which is exactly as pleasant as it sounds.

In a recent development, under that stress, the gratitude group actually became the most emotionally reactive, reporting more negative emotion than any of the other groups. And of the four groups, they were also the least likely to donate time to help others afterward.

Not exactly a Hallmark-card ending.

Does this mean we should cancel giving thanks? Of course not.

Gratitude strengthens relationships and reinforces others’ kindness. But there's a difference between privately reflecting on gratitude and sharing it.

Privately reflecting on someone's kindness can leave us with an emotional mix: appreciation, plus obligation. Expressing gratitude may not make those complicated feelings disappear. But it can offer something more: connection.

In a recent development, A study of 916 students compared four approaches: writing gratitude letters they never sent, sending personal thank-you texts, posting gratitude publicly on social media, or just tracking daily activities. Participants repeated their assigned activity four times over about a week. Those who sent personal thank-you texts showed the strongest gains in feeling connected to and supported by others.

The takeaway isn't that texting is magical. It's that gratitude may do more to strengthen feelings of being connected and supported when we share it directly with the person we're grateful for rather than keeping it to ourselves.

According to recent reports, and it may mean more to that person than we realize. In experiments by Amit Kumar and Nicholas Epley, people expressing gratitude underestimated how positive recipients would feel and overestimated how awkward they would feel.

The thank-you you’re second-guessing may land more warmly than you expect.

In my book, Micropractice: A Science-Backed Approach for Calm, Clarity, and Joy in 30 Seconds or Less, I explore in greater depth how to practice gratitude without getting caught in feelings of indebtedness, and how to weave more appreciation, connection, and joy into the moments you already have.

Here’s one small place to start.

It has been revealed that this Thanksgiving, when you feel gratitude for someone, try expressing it to them. Here’s a simple trick: Put a “you” in the sentence.

Instead of, “I’m grateful for my family," try, “Mom, you’ve always made people feel at home, even when the turkey’s running late.”.

Instead of, “I’m grateful for my friends," try, "Noor, you’re the person I call when life gets messy, and somehow you always have a way of making it lighter.”.

One describes what matters to you. The other lets someone know they matter.

Gratitude isn’t just noticing goodness. It’s letting someone know they helped create it.

This Thanksgiving, don’t just count your blessings. Let your blessings know they’re counted.

#5299. Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (810 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume.
  • Sources indicate that whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation.
  • In a recent development, to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume. Whale carcasses will sink to the bottom and become marine life habitats. Whale pee nourishes the entire ocean. But how about whale snot? The microbes and other biological material emitted from their blowholes when the giant cetaceans breathe has helped scientists sequence an entire whale genome: Take that whale vomit. The findings are detailed in a study published today in the journal Molecular Ecology Resources.

Sources indicate that whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation. With genomic data, researchers can measure population health, to see how much genetic diversity and inbreeding is present. It can also help identify individual animals for monitoring, help determine an animal’s sex, and estimate the population’s size.

In a recent development, to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy. They’ll take a dart, stick it into the whale’s blubber, and take a small sample of the skin and blubber. However, during sampling, boats must get close to the whales, which can disturb them. In some locations and for some endangered species, getting close enough to take a biopsy isn’t permitted or possible.

Sources indicate that that’s where whale snot—or blow—comes in. For this study, a team from Scotland’s University of St. Andrews, the University of Copenhagen in Denmark, the North Coast Cetacean Society, and Fisheries and Oceans Canada used several small drones off the coast of British Columbia. The drones were equipped with sterile petri dishes to collect the samples.

In a recent development, the team flew the drone through the exhaled breaths of one North pacific humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira) at a time, but still sampled several individual whales. The humpbacks generally took one to six breaths every time they surfaced—covering the drone and the dishes in whale snot.

Recent findings suggest that the team collected 58 blow samples from 26 individual humpback whales. They also took repeated samples from the same whales, collected in different encounters and across two years to match the genomes. They then cross-referenced the genomes collected from the whale blow with genomes sequenced from traditional blubber biopsies taken from the same animals.

Sources indicate that to keep the DNA from mixing, the team targeted the whale most upwind in the pod, since the blow downwind might mix with the blow from the whales up ahead. Resting whales were never sampled, and the team stopped the drone flights if a whale showed any reaction. More than one third of samples were collected by flying the drone directly from land—no boat required.

Recent findings suggest that the DNA was sequenced to produce two types of genomes. Low-coverage nuclear genomes, which are inherited from both parents, and high-coverage mitochondrial genomes, which are inherited from the mother only.

The team found that the genetic diversity estimated from the blow samples was very similar to the estimates taken from traditional biopsies. Fortunately, the humpback population in the study reveals little evidence of recent inbreeding. There is a small proportion of the genome that has long stretches of identical DNA, but the team believes that most likely reflects distant shared ancestry or past population bottlenecks.

According to the team, this research marks one of the first whole genome datasets for a group of North Pacific humpback whales. Previously, only one North Pacific humpback whole genome was publicly available.

“We will use these blow-derived genomes to not only assess population structure and health, but also assess kinship and family ties among humpback whales foraging in northern British Columbia,” Dr. Éadin O’Mahony, a study co-author and marine mammal ecologist who was at the University of St. Andrews at the time of the study, stated in a statement. “The aim is to understand how their social bonds form: Are the whales that forage together family, or long-term friends?”.

According to recent reports, as expected, the North Pacific humpback whales were genetically distinct from their counterparts living in the North Atlantic. This confirms that data taken from whale blow works as well from data taken from conventional biopsies. The drone-captured genetic analyses also correctly determined every whale’s sex, and revealed three previously undescribed mitochondrial DNA variants, which could help show how some of these whales are related. The blow from whales swimming in groups also did not have any sign of contamination from neighboring whales.

Sources indicate that about 16 percent of the DNA in each blow sample were also primarily from the microbes living in the whale’s airways. According to the team, this indicates that a single breath could tell us about the individual whale and its respiratory microbiome, opening up a potential upcoming window into cetacean health.

That’s a whole lot of data from just a little bit of snot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, is right now losing her seat.

Update: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result. As of now, with 100% of votes counted, Foxx is losing by 362 votes, but has requested a recount. We’re updating this article with the most current information on the race below.

Christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.

Foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation, and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government. Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist and native of the district.

For the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek. Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).

Christian suggested that electric cars could be incentivized with a $5,000 tax rebate – lower than the $7.5k EVs used to get, but better than the $0 they get federally today (compare to the ~$20k in ignored costs that gas cars still benefit from).

Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher, and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).

Christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who remarked “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”.

Industry observers note that but then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram, where it gained traction.

Emily noted Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”.

I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.

Foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.

Notably, none of the six links have anything to do with electric cars.

According to recent reports, in the text of the response, Foxx touts republicans’ “all of the above” energy policy, which is ironic given that the party whose energy policy she touts has spent most of the last year forcing broken dirty coal plants open (which they are still doing after ruled illegal) and trying to shut down clean cheap ones. Apparently “all of the above” is code for “fossil fuels and nothing else.”.

Industry observers note that foxx’s letter does not directly address the strengths of electric cars, despite them being the subject of Christian’s letter. Notably, EVs actually can receive energy from any generation method, whether it be wind, solar, or even coal or gas – whereas gas-powered vehicles can only use one type of energy, oil. Thus, an “all of the above” strategy should probably find EVs the preferable route for transportation.

But in apparent contradiction to Foxx’s surely sincerely held belief that we should pursue an “all of the above” energy policy – which electric cars would help to achieve – she in fact has voted against EVs when given the opportunity.

Foxx claims in her response that she can’t support tax credits on electric cars, because those go to “mostly people with higher incomes who are able to purchase ‘newly introduced’ electric cars.”.

It has been revealed that but she in fact voted against, and later voted to repeal, incentives which were limited to lower-income-earners and were only available on cars up to a certain MSRP cap. Further, they were available on used vehicles, not just new ones – suggesting that Foxx doesn’t know what she voted against.

Foxx was one of 218 republicans to vote in favor of a ~$4 trillion giveaway to wealthy elites. Her vote raised electric bills and threatened US energy security and surrendered US manufacturing jobs to China. Some of the money given away to wealthy elites in the bill was clawed back from energy efficiency programs that had been going to regular Americans.

According to recent reports, those energy efficiency programs had been instituted by the Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era law which established tax credits for EVs and other efficiency rebates. The Inflation Reduction Act was actually revenue positive, which is to say it reduced the national debt (by $238B), rather than adding to it, because of provisions to increase enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.

According to recent reports, but most of the IRA was repealed by the bill that Foxx voted for, meaning the US lost out on those deficit reductions. All in all, the bill Foxx voted for would add $4 trillion to the national debt – which, incidentally, is another point Foxx touches on in her response.

In one sentence, she seems to directly mock Christian, telling him that “YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt” as part of a warning about the dangers of government debt.

According to recent reports, but I read this sentence as mockery, rather than as a sincere warning, given that Foxx voted to add $4 trillion to the national debt, which she, at 83 years old, knows she will not have to pay off. Christian, who is 10, will likely spend his whole life saddled with the debt Foxx voted for.

According to recent reports, he will also have to pay for her inaction on climate change, which will have increasingly worse effects on the world Christian will grow up into. Foxx’s generation has already felt the heat, with the massive floods that devastated her state in 2024, from a hurricane that was made 200x more likely due to climate change. Now, imagine how much worse it could get if Foxx’s policies remained in place until 72 years from now when Christian will be her age.

Foxx then closes out the letter with disparaging remarks about teachers, claiming that they are “too interested in indoctrinating you,” and warning Christian about “propaganda.” Which I guess shows where Foxx’s attitude comes from – if she has spent her 83 years never trusting anyone who knows more than her about a topic, that would certainly lead to the ignorance reflected in her letter.

Foxx – who somehow has a doctorate in education and currently sits on the Congressional education committee – could have turned this into a nice moment to teach the child who wrote her something about democracy and responsive government, but instead turned it into a moment to teach the world what’s wrong with her.

When we first wrote this article, Foxx had a projected 97% chance of winning in a district which voted for her by a 19% margin in 2024.

But that was before America (and its short memory) was reminded of how incapable republicans are of leading anything.

Recent findings suggest that after a pile of economic crises caused by Donald Trump’s incompetent “leadership,” and his continued participation in an 8-month-and-counting war of choice that is spiking energy prices worldwide, bringing oil profits to record highs (and attempting to distract the news from talking about the Epstein files, which he is heavily featured in and has tried to cover up), America was once again fed up. And his incompetence took his entire party down with him.

Safe republican seats were flipped around the country in the biggest “wave” election we’ve seen in recent times, with the Democrats gaining control of both the House and Senate.

And it looks like Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a Wilkes county native and former journalist, who also ran against Foxx in 2024, will now get his chance to represent the people of North Carolina’s 5th district… assuming a recount goes in his favor.

The situation in North Carolina is particularly interesting, given that republicans had done an emergency redraw of district lines in an attempt to cheat their way to winning more seats.

In a recent development, generally, district lines get redrawn after each Census, which happens on the decade mark, rather than mid-decade. But republicans saw ahead of time that they were likely to lose the House due to their unpopularity, and wanted to fudge the numbers in several states instead of going for a fair fight.

According to recent reports, foxx’s main argument against Christian’s suggested $5,000 EV incentive, is increasing national debt. Yet in just one tax bill, her approval increases the national debt over 10%. This is not Christian’s “responsibility”, this burden is forced on him, along with climate change.

In a recent development, so they engaged in Gerrymandering, a process wherein district lines are redrawn to favor a particular political party. The idea is to put as many of your opponents’ votes into a few safe seats as possible, while spreading out your own votes to a wider range of seats that you win each by a small margin.

But it turns out that republicans were even more unpopular than they thought, and as a result, their Gerrymandering backfired. Those narrow margins they sought ended up flipping more seats than would have otherwise flipped, turning North Carolina almost completely blue in what analysts have called a “Dummymander“. (NC-5 itself was not one of the redrawn districts, though – it just swung 19 whole points to the Dems).

That said: the race is not over yet. The deadline to request a recount is today, and sure enough, Foxx has done so. The current margin is extremely thin, just 0.12% of votes, so things could certainly change in a recount. Foxx also vowed to run again in 2028, hoping for a less hostile political environment. She will be 85 years old at the time of that election.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that BMW issued a “Park Outside” warning as part of a recall that covers nearly three-quarters of a million vehicles and includes a fire risk warning. The recall covers 720,796 vehicles ranging from the 2012 through the 2018 model years. The recall population includes some 3-series, 5-series, Z4, X1, X3, X4, X5 xDrive40e, 4-series Gran Coupe, 2-series convertible, 328xi Gran Turismo, 2-series coupe, 4-series convertible, 3-series coupe, and 3-series Sportswagon vehicles.

In a recent development, the concern is centered on a connector for the water pump, which, over time, could deteriorate and allow moisture to enter the pump. If moisture enters the connector, it could result in a short circuit, which in turn could cause a vehicle fire.

See all results for used 2016 BMW 3-series for sale near 29405.

The recall follows a similar recall issued on August 13, 2024, which also centered on the water pump. The remedy for that recall involved a protective shield to divert any residual fluid from the engine’s positive crankcase ventilation system’s air intake hose to keep it from entering the water pump’s electrical connector. Unfortunately, after that recall was performed, BMW was made aware of several instances of pump failures on vehicles that had the remedy performed. At the time of this newer recall, the firm is aware of 10 field instances in the United States believed to be related to the glitch.

According to recent reports, the automaker is still working on a permanent fix for the affected vehicles. Dealer notification letters have already been sent, with interim owner notification letters scheduled to be sent on December 25. Owners concerned that their vehicle may be included in the recall population will have to wait until that day to search for their VIN.

Tech Report: Healthier Salt Substitute May Prevent Millions of Deaths From Heart Disease

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, new research suggests.
  • In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.
  • They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million new cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, new research suggests.

In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.

They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million new cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.

In the United States, this simple salt swap could prevent nearly 105,000 deaths and about 492,000 new cases a year, the researchers estimated.

In a recent development, about 130.6 million U.S. adults have cardiovascular disease, according to the American Heart Association (AHA).

Liping Huang, PhD, a senior data analyst in the Food Policy Division at The George Institute for Global Health and co-lead author of the study, told Healthline the team started with current blood pressure levels by sex, age, and country.

The researchers then estimated how replacing all salt with a salt substitute would change people’s sodium and potassium intake, blood pressure, and disease risk, she noted.The team modeled a blend of 75% sodium chloride and 25% potassium chloride. The study estimated these yearly results worldwide:.

The authors wrote that the model relied on data from a few years ago and on many assumptions, and that any large-scale switch would take years.

Potassium-enriched salt replaces some of the sodium chloride in regular table salt with potassium chloride, according to The George Institute.Asked where other salts like kosher salt and sea salt fit in, Huang mentioned those salts may contain some trace elements “which has those health halos around them, but essentially they’re still primarily sodium chloride.”Huang noted that potassium-enriched salt tastes “about the same as a regular table salt.” She said it’s possible a small number of people with a sensitive palate could taste a difference.

Huang remarked that “it’s really hard for people to cut back their salt intake.”“But the easier way is just to replace part of the sodium chloride in our normal salt with potassium chloride, because increasing potassium intake also helps to reduce blood pressure,” she said.The two minerals play opposite roles in the body, according to Cheng-Han Chen, MD, a board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“While sodium causes water retention and increased blood pressure, potassium will help the kidneys remove sodium from the body and lower blood pressure,” Chen told Healthline.Huang noted she worked on an earlier trial of about 21,000 people in 600 rural villages in northern China in 2021.

People who used potassium-enriched salt had a 14% lower risk of stroke, a 13% lower risk of cardiovascular events, and a 12% lower risk of early death than those who used regular salt, according to a 2021 study in The New England Journal of Medicine that summarized the trial’s results.

The World Health Organization (WHO) endorsed potassium-enriched salt in a 2025 guideline, saying it can reduce blood pressure and the risk of cardiovascular disease.

Recent findings suggest that the AHA noted potassium-based salt substitutes can help lower blood pressure in some adults. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued labeling guidance in 2020 allowing an alternate name for potassium chloride on ingredient labels to include the word “salt.”“We think that blood pressure begins to improve as soon as 1 week after cutting back on sodium intake. The full benefit typically takes up to 4 weeks,” Chen said.

It has been revealed that “We generally recommend a daily sodium limit of 2,300 milligrams (mg), ideally under 1,500 mg a day. Most people consume over 3,000 mg of sodium a day, well above the recommended limit,” Chen noted.The WHO recommends less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day and suggests at least 3,510 mg of potassium a day.In the United States, more than 70% of salt intake comes from processed and restaurant foods, according to the AHA.

In a recent development, huang said that some people with advanced chronic kidney disease should avoid potassium-enriched salt.When the kidneys don’t work well, the body may not clear extra potassium efficiently, she said. That can lead to hyperkalemia, or high potassium levels in the blood, which can raise the risk of cardiac arrest, Huang said.Among people with stage 3 to stage 5 kidney disease, switching to salt substitutes could prevent about 750,000 deaths a year by lowering blood pressure and cause about 100,000 deaths a year from hyperkalemia, the researchers estimated.The AHA said that people with kidney disease or who take medications that affect potassium should check with a healthcare professional before using these products.

According to recent reports, an estimated 37 million U.S. adults have chronic kidney disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Potassium-enriched salt is available at supermarkets in the U.S. Many major U.S. grocery chains, including Kroger, Walmart, and Publix, carry two types of products, according to their websites:.

Potassium-enriched salt typically costs about twice as much as regular salt, according to the study.Huang mentioned she hoped people would see the results and start thinking of the switch as “a simple thing I can do for their own health.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there’s no shortage of rare, collectable, crazy-desirable classic Mercedes-Benz vehicles out there for the discerning car collector. Some of the Three-Pointed Star’s cars have gone down in history among the most expensive automobiles ever sold; there’s the $11.8 million 1936 Mercedes-Benz 540 K Special Roadster by Sindelfingen, the $10.2 million 2002 Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR Roadster, and of course, the 1955 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé that sold for over $140 million back in 2022, making it the world’s most valuable car.

In a recent development, but no matter how rich, how connected, how much of a master of the universe you are, you’ve never been able to buy one of Mercedes-Benz’s most ground-breaking machines: the rotary-powered C111. Or at least, that was the case. Come next year, for the very first time, one lucky person will be able to take the Apollo-era wundercar home.

It has been revealed that fans of the brand certainly need no introduction to this wedge-shaped beauty, but for those of you who might not be as current on your Mercedes history, the C111 was revealed at the 1969 International Motor Show (IAA) in Frankfurt, less than two months after Neil Armstrong plopped his boots on the moon. The idea was to create a gullwinged successor to the iconic W198-gen 300SL that dominated racing in the 1950s, packed with then-impressive technology: Wankel rotary engines, fiberglass bodywork, and multi-link rear suspension, all wrapped in a gorgeous period design.

Yet while 17 prototypes were ultimately made, the car never entered production. Rumor has it that interested parties practically channeled Philip J. Fry shouting “Shut up and take my money” by mailing blank checks to the company’s home office, but Mercedes remarked no dice, citing the Wankel motor’s inability to play nicely with the 1973 oil crisis. (That also kept the motor from winding up in the S-Class, as Mercedes-Benz Classic head of collection Dennis Heck said.) Instead, the copies served as company test beds for years, performing tasks like high-speed testing at Nardo with a variety of different powertrains and aerodynamic kits.

In a recent development, the car in question that will be up for grabs is the third one ever made, a C111-II variant known internally as “Car 33” that comes equipped with its original 2.4-liter 4-rotor engine making 345 horsepower and 289 lb-ft connected to a 5-speed manual gearbox. It was used as part of the Mercedes test fleet, trialing features like anti-lock brakes and a component to empty its twin fuel tanks at even rates—a handy feature in a car capable of 186 miles per hour.

According to recent reports, the car was restored to working order two years ago at the Mercedes-Benz Classic Center, although the patina of the Weißherbst-colored exterior and gray-and-white houndstooth patterned interior was kept delightfully intact. As of last month’s photo shoot, its odometer showed 24,766 kilometers—15,355 miles.

The C111 in question will hit the auction block on February 3, 2027, at the Palais du Louvre as part of RM Sotheby’s Retromobile Paris auctions, with the funds raised by the sale used to help the automaker further develop the Mercedes-Benz museum in Stuttgart, including the creation of a digital twin of the museum that will let people access it virtually.

Given its provenance, I would not expect it to go cheap. Neither does the organization. “We do believe it will come to a significant double-digit euro [price at auction],” CEO of Mercedes-Benz Heritage GmbH Marcus Breitschwerdt told Road & Track.

According to recent reports, “It’s gonna be in excess of twenty-five [million] euros,” RM Sotheby’s president Gord Duff added. “There will be strong activity. It’s one of those things you could never get until now.”.

Recent findings suggest that and if you’re thinking, Ehh, they’ve broken the seal on sales, I’ll wait until they auction off another one—well, you’d better be prepared to hold off until 2051 or so, because Mercedes says this sale includes a contractual commitment that it will not sell any more C111s for the next 25 years. Should you be interested in bidding, you can find out more here.

  • Despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.

The one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee. I am so hopelessly addicted to the stuff that I usually need at least one cup of coffee before going out to meet a friend for coffee.

Despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health. Throughout my lifetime, coffee has variously been purported to protect my heart, disrupt its rhythm, reduce my risk of cancer, and increase it. All I know is it helps me become a fully conscious person every morning. But could my coffee habit actually reduce wrinkles and help me age more gracefully?

A newly introduced study conducted at Texas A&M suggests that certain compounds in coffee might protect the body against aging and inflammation.

However, according to Dr. Dung Trinh, the chief medical officer at Healthy Brain Clinic in Long Beach, California, it’s probably too soon to pop open the champagne (or brew a celebratory pot) over the potential perks of your coffee habit.

“It’s far too early to treat coffee—or caffeic acid—as an anti-aging intervention,” Trinh tells Popular Science.

Recent findings suggest that despite its inconsistent status as a health food, coffee has been consistently linked to longer life and a lower likelihood of certain diseases, though it’s not certain why. The Texas A&M study, led by Dr. Stephen Safe, focused on a cellular receptor called NR4A1.

NR4A1 is a protein that regulates how cells respond to stress and damage. The study found that several compounds in coffee, particularly polyphenols—plant compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties—bind to the NR4A1 receptor. One of these polyphenols, caffeic acid, is found in coffee and many other plants and, despite its name, has nothing to do with caffeine. These compounds seem to promote NR4A1’s protective effects, including mitigating cellular damage and slowing the growth of cancer cell line in laboratory models.

Industry observers note that in other words, the harder your NR4A1 proteins are working, the better your cells may be at fending off damage. Sign me up!

Recent findings suggest that after researchers removed NR4A1 from cells in the lab, those benefits stopped, suggesting this receptor may help produce them. So, if coffee really helps NR4A1 do its job, we might just have a new anti-aging drink on our hands.

Interestingly, caffeine does not appear to play a key part in this mechanism, Trinh states. Instead, those benefits seem to come from coffee’s other compounds, like caffeic acid and its fellow polyphenols.

“What stood out to me was that the story was not really about caffeine,” he states. “I also found it interesting that the researchers did more than simply show that these compounds could bind to the receptor—they demonstrated NR4A1-dependent effects in cells. That makes the mechanism more compelling.”.

Translation: The study didn’t just show that coffee compounds attach to NR4A1; it showed that this binding actually seems to activate the protein’s protective effects.

Consistent with this, the study also found that decaf coffee demonstrated similar protective effects on the lab cells, providing further evidence that coffee’s benefits may not have anything to do with caffeine at all.

“One of the interesting messages from this paper is that coffee should not be thought of as simply a delivery system for caffeine,” Trinh notes. “Caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid, ferulic acid, and several other coffee compounds all interacted with NR4A1, while caffeine highlighted much more variable NR4A1-related activity.”.

So, coffee’s superpower might not come from caffeine at all, at least when it comes to anti-aging benefits.

Before you start guzzling triple lattes in the name of cellular protection, know that “more” does not always mean “better.”.

According to recent reports, “We simply cannot infer from this study that more coffee means more NR4A1 benefit,” Trinh says. This is because the researchers studied coffee extracts and purified compounds in a lab setting rather than giving human subjects increasing amounts of coffee and measuring NR4A1 activity. Plus, in human biology, it’s possible to have too much of a good thing, Trinh says.

Sources indicate that “At some point, additional coffee can bring unwanted effects from caffeine, including sleep disruption, anxiety, palpitations, or increases in blood pressure in susceptible people,” he notes. “Those effects could counteract other health benefits. So, this study should not be interpreted as establishing either an optimal number of cups or a dose-response relationship for this pathway.”.

Trinh adds that as compelling as the study’s findings are, he doesn’t yet believe they justify changing recommendations around coffee consumption.

Earlier studies have linked coffee drinking to living longer and to better outcomes for some age-related conditions, Trinh claims. But those studies couldn’t explain why. This one offers “one possible biological explanation,” he says.

Industry observers note that like most early-stage research, Trinh says, this study can’t be applied to humans sipping their morning “cup of ambition.” Much of the work used a specific cancer cell in the lab, along with mouse immune cells, rather than testing regular human coffee drinkers directly. And while the study identified a potentially promising mechanism, it’s not clear how this mechanism will translate to human health outcomes.

Ultimately, Trinh says, no single food or compound is likely to be the deciding factor in how well we age.

It has been revealed that for a coffee addict like myself, though, these findings are the best kind of wake-up call. Coffee may or may not turn back the clock, but it does stop me from hitting snooze 15 times.

“The much bigger determinants of healthy aging remain things such as regular physical activity, good sleep, avoiding smoking, controlling blood pressure and metabolic risk, maintaining social and cognitive engagement, and eating an overall nutritious diet,” Trinh says.

“This study is a promising piece of the scientific puzzle, not a prescription for another cup of coffee.”.

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its fresh Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-fresh iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the firm’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the fresh battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the company is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We said we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A organization spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

The 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

Sources indicate that it features BMW’s new “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW noted you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW said enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

The electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW notes it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

In a recent development, inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a latest 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

This is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

Edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s fresh iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

It has been revealed that by 2030, BMW aims to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, mentioned.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

#5292. When Therapy Forgets What It Means to Be Human

When Therapy Forgets What It Means to Be Human

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (943 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • These days, when you hear mental health professionals say that they want clients to understand their conditions better, they are usually referring to diagnostic labels.
  • Industry observers note that if you want to understand why you are feeling down, the thinking goes, you need to understand depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

These days, when you hear mental health professionals say that they want clients to understand their conditions better, they are usually referring to diagnostic labels. It is a shame how much mental health conditions have been reduced to labels.

Industry observers note that if you want to understand why you are feeling down, the thinking goes, you need to understand depression. If you are nervous about things that are happening in your life, you need to understand anxiety. If you are having difficulties in social situations, you need to understand autism. And if your mood tends to fluctuate easily, you need to understand bipolar disorder.

Recent findings suggest that what makes this even more troubling is how much these conditions are reduced not just to labels, but to labels related only to physical functioning. When it comes to mental health problems, the questions are often reduced to labels, and human beings are reduced to physiological machines.

In a recent development, it is almost as if people are treated as robots. Understand what is going wrong with a robot’s mechanics, and you can fix it.

But what if your psychological condition is just part of being human?

What if your depression is due to a lack of meaning or purpose in life? What if your anxiety is due to a very real fear caused by life being uncertain? What if your difficulties with people are due to the negative ways people act toward you, or uncertainty because social interactions do not come with any sort of guidebook? And what if your fluctuating mood is related to recognizing that you have a limited time on earth and are trying to find the best ways of navigating obstacles toward making that time meaningful?

Industry observers note that for example, think about someone who comes to counseling feeling depressed because they spent years working toward goals that no longer seem meaningful. They may be having difficulty sleeping, have little motivation, and feel sad much of the time. Those symptoms might justify a depression diagnosis, but does that diagnosis really explain what the person is experiencing?

Understanding the person's struggle with meaning and purpose may be much more vital than simply saying they have depression and need to understand that diagnosis better. Saying “you’re searching for more meaning and purpose in your life” fits more with what it means to be human than saying “you have depression.”.

It is unfortunate that authors, artists, and philosophers recognize that being human involves functioning on multiple deep levels, but psychologists and counselors often do not.

Life is difficult. Life is complex. Navigating that complexity can be difficult, troubling, and emotionally taxing. Feeling like something is missing, something is lost, something is difficult to navigate, or something is meaningless can be a very real source of emotional distress.

Yet mental health professionals may not recognize this.

Medical thinking and pharmaceutical companies seem to dominate mental healthcare to a large degree, and this can lead to minimizing or abandoning altogether the idea that human beings can experience true emotional distress because they are looking for their lives to have direction, meaning, and purpose and just cannot find it.

Sources indicate that none of this means that physiology, neurology, or medication should be ignored. It means that understanding these things is not the same as understanding a human being.

If you are seeking a therapist or counselor, this is something to keep in mind. Does the therapist or counselor reduce your suffering to just physiology or something wrong with your body or neurology? Do they seem to act primarily as a cheerleader for pharmaceutical companies, where the answer keeps coming back to medication? Or do they truly look at the complexities of what you are facing in your life?

If there is a lot of focus in your therapy or counseling on physiology and medication, this does not mean that your counselor or therapist is doing something wrong. But it may be worth bringing up. Asking your therapist or counselor whether there is room to discuss deeper questions in life can be an crucial step for moving therapy in a more helpful direction. It is important to consider whether you are truly being treated as a human being and not just a machine.

Recent findings suggest that if we compare ourselves to machines, we know that human beings function on a much more complex level. Machines do not worry about meaning or purpose in their lives. Machines may recognize that they have an expiration date, but they do not worry about getting certain things done within that timeframe. Machines understand the tasks ahead of them and work on those tasks until the time they shut down, but they do not worry about what it means if they do not get those tasks done.

Human beings worry about living purposeful lives and filling their lives with meaning. Human beings feel lost when things that seem crucial are missing from their lives. Machines do not. They may recognize that things are missing as a fact, but they do not have any sort of emotional response to it.

Saying that, as a human being, you are not a machine may sound like a cliché. But it is really unfortunate when you look at how often human beings are treated as machines.

As a human being, it may often be up to you to speak up and say, "Treat me as a human, not as a machine.".

Even Alaska’s bears are not immune from accidentally making things weird or getting a bit too close. Over the summer, rangers at Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska watched an odd interaction between two unnamed black bears (Ursus americanus) taking part in Anan Creek’s salmon run.

Industry observers note that “Sometimes the bears at Anan share the creek… a little too closely,” the rangers write. “One bear is waiting his turn for a prime fishing spot, and the other is so focused on the fish he doesn’t mind his surroundings. Did the 1st bear make it weird by backing up, or did the 2nd bear make it weird by staying there?”.

For this bit of humor, the rangers awarded the unnamed bears with the 2026 You Made it Weird Award.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

The largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in the region. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

💡 Key Takeaways
